label: Scaling, Performance & Operations
desc: 17 interview questions covering Scaling, Sharding, Transactions, Indexing and more.

subs.label: Scaling
subs.desc: MongoDB scales the same way any distributed application would: throw more resources at a single machine (vertical scaling) or distribute the data across multiple physical servers or nodes (horizontal scaling).

subs.label: Sharding
subs.desc: MongoDB supports horizontal scaling through sharding — a method for distributing data across multiple machines, used for deployments with very large datasets and high throughput.

subs.label: Transactions
subs.desc: A write operation is atomic at the level of a single document, even if it modifies multiple embedded documents within that one document.

subs.label: Indexing
subs.desc: Where should you use an index in MongoDB? How would you choose an indexing strategy in MongoDB, and what should you consider?

subs.label: Reliability
subs.desc: How does MongoDB ensure data consistency and reliability?

subs.desc: What are MongoDB's backup and restore options?

subs.label: Concurrency

subs.desc: What security features does MongoDB offer?

subs.label: Atlas
subs.desc: MongoDB Atlas is the cloud-hosted database-as-a-service (DBaaS) platform for MongoDB.
